I havn't checked the original example, you might contact Michela.C about
his.

these models are somewhat flexible, and you can certainly make them a
good fit to the data. It think there are updated versions of this models
which make use of the Penalized Complexity priors, which makes it easier
to avoid overfitting.

Best
H

On Thu, 2021-04-22 at 11:40 -0700, Siddharth Rawat wrote:
> Hi,
> I am trying to fit a Spatio-temporal  Gaussian model. I have followed
> this paper to code:
> https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/case-studies/Cameletti2012/Cameletti_et_al_2012_acc.pdf.Below
> is the code for my model:
>
>
> locs <- unique(full_training2[, c("long", "lat")])
>
> mesh2 <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = locs, offset = c(5, 20), max.edge =
> c(40,100) , min.angle=c(21,21))
>
> spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh2)
> field.indices = inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=spde$n.spde,
> n.group=max(df$wk_num))
>
> ## Link data and process
> A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh2, loc = cbind(full_training2$long,
> full_training2$lat), group = full_training2$wk_num, n.group =
> max(df$wk_num))
>
> stack.est = inla.stack(data = list(y = full_training2$log_prevalence),
> A = list(A,1), effects = list(c(field.indices,list(Intercept=1)),
>                                                                       
>                           
> list(full_training2[,c("population","time","time_sq","prev_log_new_dea
> th")])), tag="est")
>
> ## the model
> formula = y ~ -1 + log(population)  + time + time_sq +
> prev_log_new_death + f(field, model = spde,
> group=field.group,control.group = list(model =
> "exchangeable"))#,control.group = list(model = "rw1")
>
>
> A.pred = inla.spde.make.A(mesh2, loc=cbind(testing$long,
> testing$lat),group=testing$wk_num,
> n.group=max(df$wk_num))#,group=testing$wk_num, n.group=n_tmp_testing)
>
> field.indices.pred = inla.spde.make.index("field", n.spde=spde$n.spde,
> n.group=max(df$wk_num) )
>
> stack.pred = inla.stack(data=list(y =
> NA),A=list(A.pred,1),effects=list(c(field.indices.pred,
> list(Intercept=1)),list(testing[,c("population","time","time_sq","prev
> _log_new_death")])),tag="pred")#,list(Intercept=1)
>
>
> stack = inla.stack(stack.est, stack.pred)
>
> #computing only hyperparameters
> hyper_mod <- inla(formula, data=inla.stack.data(stack.est, spde=spde),
> family="gaussian",
>             control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack.est),
> compute=FALSE))
>
> inla_mod = inla(formula, data=inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde),
> family="gaussian",
>                 control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), 
> compute=TRUE,link=1),
>                 control.mode=list(theta = hyper_mod$mode$theta,
> restart=FALSE))
>
> index.pred = inla.stack.index(stack,"pred")$data
>
> index.est = inla.stack.index(stack,"est")$data
>
> MAPE_inla = (sum(abs( (y_testing -
> inla_mod$summary.fitted.values[index.pred, "mean"])/y_testing
> )))/n_testing
>
> R_sq_inla = 1 - sum((y_full_training2 -
> inla_mod$summary.fitted.values[index.est,
> "mean"])^2)/sum((y_full_training2 - mean(y_full_training2))^2)
>
> ###################################################
> I am getting a R_Sq_value of 0.995.
> Is there anything wrong with my model?
